'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Gaza–Israel conflict]]
**Three [[Palestinian people|Palestinian]] fishermen are killed in an explosion off the coast of [[Gaza Strip|Gaza]]. The blast is caused by an unknown weapon, suspected to be a [[rocket]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/3/7/three-palestinian-fishermen-killed-in-explosion-off-gaza-coast (Al Jazeera English)]
*[[2021 Myanmar coup d'état]]
**Khin Maung Latt, a campaign manager from [[Aung San Suu Kyi]]’s [[National League for Democracy]], dies in [[Myanmar Police Force|police]] custody after being arrested yesterday. [https://amp.scmp.com/news/asia/southeast-asia/article/3124400/frustrated-and-fed-journalists-group-calls-release (''South China Morning Post'')]
*[[Saudi Arabian-led intervention in Yemen]]
**In retaliation for yesterday's [[drone attack]]s against the kingdom, the [[Saudi Arabia|Saudi]]-led coalition conducts [[airstrike]]s against the [[Houthis]] in the Yemeni capital [[Sanaa]]. There have been no reports of any immediate casualties. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-yemen-security-saudi/saudi-led-coalition-launches-air-strikes-on-yemeni-capital-after-foiling-drone-attacks-witness-idUSKBN2AZ03F?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[United States Secretary of Defense|U.S. Defense Secretary]] [[Lloyd Austin]] says that the [[United States]] will continue to defend troops and interests. He also says that those who carried out the [[2021 Erbil missile attacks|rocket attack]] in [[Iraq]] will be held accountable. [https://www.cnbc.com/2021/03/07/us-will-defend-troops-after-rocket-attack-in-iraq-lloyd-austin-says.html (CNBC)]
*Nine activists are killed in [[Philippine National Police|police]] raids in the northern [[Philippines]] two days after [[President of the Philippines|President]] [[Rodrigo Duterte]] ordered [[Government of the Philippines|government]] [[Armed Forces of the Philippines|forces]] to kill [[Communism|communists]] in the country. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/3/7/philippines-deadly-operation-after-order-to-kill-communists (Al Jazeera English)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2021 Bata explosions]]
**A series of explosions kill 20 people and injure more than 600 others in [[Bata, Equatorial Guinea|Bata]], [[Equatorial Guinea]]. The cause is suspected to be negligence related to use of dynamite at a local military base. Almost all buildings in the city are heavily damaged. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/3/7/four-large-explosions-hit-equatorial-guinea-city-of-bata-reports (Al Jazeera English)]
*A fire occurs at a detention center for migrants in [[Sanaa]], [[Yemen]], killing at least eight people and injuring more than 170 others. [https://abcnews.go.com/International/wireStory/fire-yemeni-migrant-detention-center-kills-76310149 (ABC News)]
*At least one person is killed and 40 others are injured when a train [[derailment|derails]] in [[Sindh]], [[Pakistan]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/3/7/dozens-injured-as-train-derails-in-southwest-pakistan (Al Jazeera English)]
*A [[Eurocopter AS350 Écureuil]] crashes in [[Normandy]], [[France]], killing [[National Assembly (France)|National Assembly]] member and businessman [[Olivier Dassault]] and the aircraft's pilot. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2021/mar/07/french-billionaire-politician-olivier-dassault-dies-in-helicopter-crash (''The Guardian'')]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Oceania]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]]
****[[COVID-19 vaccination in Australia]]
*****Former [[Prime Minister of Australia|Prime Minister]] [[Julia Gillard]] and current [[Minister for Health and Aged Care|Health Minister]] [[Greg Hunt]] receive their first doses of the [[Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine|Oxford–AstraZeneca]] [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]]. [https://www.9news.com.au/national/coronavirus-astrazeneca-vaccinations-begin-in-wa-today-as-federal-government-reveals-timetable-for-gps/a1a38265-0ee1-41c9-b4a5-592c830f0182 (''Nine News'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in New Caledonia]]
****[[New Caledonia]] orders a strict [[COVID-19 lockdowns|lockdown]] for two weeks beginning at midnight tomorrow following the detection of nine [[COVID-19]] cases among non-quarantined travellers arriving from [[Wallis and Futuna]]. [https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20210307-french-new-caledonia-island-group-faces-two-week-lockdown-as-covid-finally-hits (Radio France Internationale)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in New Zealand]]
****[[Auckland]] is downgraded to alert level 2 while the rest of [[New Zealand]] moves to alert level 1 following confirmation that there are no more community cases. [https://i.stuff.co.nz/national/health/coronavirus/300246527/no-new-community-cases-as-auckland-shifts-to-covid19-alert-level-2-rest-of-nz-moves-to-level-1 (Stuff)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Israel]]
****[[Israel]] reopens restaurants, bars, and other entertainment venues for those who have been vaccinated against COVID-19. Middle-school students return to school in some areas and university classes also resume for those who have been vaccinated. Israeli citizens are also allowed to return to Israel without any special permissions. [https://www.haaretz.com/israel-news/israel-reopens-restaurants-pubs-event-venues-for-those-vaccinated-against-covid-1.9596374 (''Haaretz'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia]]
****At age 95, former [[Prime Minister of Malaysia|Prime Minister]] [[Mahathir Mohamad]] becomes the oldest person in [[Malaysia]] to [[National COVID-19 Immunisation Programme (Malaysia)|receive a dose]] of the COVID-19 vaccine in [[Langkawi]], [[Kedah]]. [https://www.malaysiakini.com/news/565677?fbclid=IwAR3S-FPhc5Aql3ZhRolnpZ1Geuo8qM2wvRHR01Zo4LhfdVRZIr3tIufKKJs (''Malaysiakini'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Nepal]]
****[[Nepal]] receives 348,000 doses of the [[Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine|Oxford–AstraZeneca]] vaccine supplied through the [[COVAX]] vaccine-sharing initiative. [https://kathmandupost.com/visual-stories/2021/03/07/nepal-receives-348-000-doses-of-covid-19-vaccine-under-who-s-covax-facility (''The Kathmandu Post'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Sri Lanka]]
****[[Sri Lanka]] receives its first shipment of 264,000 doses of the [[Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine|Oxford–AstraZeneca]] vaccine supplied through the COVAX vaccine-sharing initiative. [https://www.newindianexpress.com/world/2021/mar/07/sri-lanka-receives-oxford-astrazeneca-vaccines-under-covax-facility-2273429.html (''The New Indian Express'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Austria]]
****[[Austria]] suspends vaccinations using the [[Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine|Oxford–AstraZeneca]] [[vaccine]] as a precaution while investigating the death of a person who received it. [https://www.irishtimes.com/news/world/europe/covid-19-austria-suspends-batch-of-astrazeneca-vaccine-as-precaution-after-death-1.4503567 (''The Irish Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in North Macedonia]]
****[[North Macedonia]] grants emergency use authorization for [[Russia]]'s [[Sputnik V COVID-19 vaccine|Sputnik V]] vaccine. [https://finance.yahoo.com/news/north-macedonia-approves-russias-sputnik-093000388.html (Yahoo! Finance)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Slovakia]], [[501.V2 variant]]
****[[Slovakia]] reports its first seven cases of the 501.V2 variant first detected in [[South Africa]]. [https://spectator.sme.sk/c/22612119/south-africa-variant-confirmed-in-slovakia.html (''The Slovak Spectator'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Ohio]], [[Lineage P.1]]
****[[Ohio]] reports its first cases of the Lineage P.1 variant first detected in [[Brazil]]. [https://www.cincinnati.com/story/news/2021/03/07/ohio-coronavirus-covid-19-variant-p-1-brazil/4623462001/ (''The Cincinnati Enquirer'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Ethiopia]]
***[[Ethiopia]] receives its first shipment of 2.2 million doses of the [[Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine|Oxford–AstraZeneca]] vaccine manufactured by the [[Serum Institute of India]] supplied through the COVAX vaccine-sharing initiative. [https://www.barrons.com/articles/ethiopia-gears-up-for-covid-vaccine-drive-as-first-doses-arrive-01615110604 (''Barron's'')]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2021 Swiss referendums]]
**[[Swiss people|Swiss]] voters approve a ban on full-facial coverings in public, known popularly as a so-called "[[burqa]] ban", and a [[free trade agreement]] with [[Indonesia]], while rejecting a government proposal to introduce nationwide electronic IDs, which would be required to open a [[bank account]] or request official documents. [https://www.npr.org/2021/03/07/974630640/switzerland-approves-ban-on-face-coverings-in-public?t=1615207930951 (NPR)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2020–21 Scottish Premiership]]
**[[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] wins the [[Scottish Premiership]], the top-flight league in [[Football in Scotland|Scottish football]], for the first time since 2011 after their rivals [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] failed to win against [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]]. It is Rangers manager and former England captain [[Steven Gerrard]]'s first trophy as a manager, and the win also denies Celtic a record 10th consecutive Premiership title. [https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/56306235 (BBC Sport)]
*[[2021 FC Barcelona presidential election]]
**Former [[FC Barcelona]] president [[Joan Laporta]] wins the club's 14th presidential election with 54.2% of the votes. [https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11833/12239526/joan-laporta-wins-barcelona-presidential-election-by-landslide-over-victor-font-and-toni-freixa (Sky Sports)]
